firefox-extension-ruffle-nightly is built from ruffle-nightly

Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope contains only variable assignments, array definitions, and a conditional that appends to `makedepends` — none of which execute arbitrary code or network requests. The `pkgver` is a simple variable expansion, not a function that downloads or runs anything. The `source` array fetches a single git repository from the official upstream (`git+https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle.git`), which is the expected project source. The `chromium-extension-ruffle.key` entry present in the first `source` definition is overwritten by the second and thus has no effect. All potentially dangerous operations — `cargo install`, `npm ci`, `npm run build:repro`, command substitutions involving `tomlq`/`git rev-parse`/`date` — reside inside `prepare()`, `build()`, and `check()` functions, which are explicitly skipped by the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags. The two commands in question (`makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`) will only source the PKGBUILD and fetch the upstream git repository, neither of which contains malicious payloads.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>No malicious code executes during source fetch or PKGBUILD sourcing.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is for the Ruffle Flash Player emulator (nightly build) and follows standard AUR packaging practices. The script fetches the official ruffle-rs repository from GitHub, builds it with cargo/npm, and installs the Firefox extension, Chromium extension, and related components to standard system locations.

All network interactions are to expected upstream sources: cloning from `github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle`, npm registry for dependencies, cargo registry for Rust crates, and Google's official CRX update endpoint (`clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx`) for the Chromium extension manifest. No suspicious commands like `curl|bash`, `eval`, `base64` decoding, or unexpected remote code execution patterns are present. The package does not exfiltrate data, modify unrelated system files, or install backdoors.

Note: There is a duplicate `source=` line that effectively overwrites the first, dropping `chromium-extension-ruffle.key` from the source array — this is a packaging bug, not malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence/>
<summary>Legitimate AUR package for Ruffle emulator; no malicious code detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>
This is an `.SRCINFO` metadata file for the `firefox-extension-ruffle-nightly` AUR package. It contains only package metadata (dependencies, sources, descriptions) and no executable build functions. The sole source is `git+https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle.git#tag=nightly-2026-08-27`, which fetches from the project's official upstream repository on GitHub — this is expected and normal. The package defines multiple sub-packages (desktop app, demo web app, self-hosted JS module, Firefox extension, Chromium extension), which is a standard multi-package AUR structure. There are no suspicious network destinations, no obfuscated code, no dangerous commands (curl, wget, eval, base64), and no signs of tampering or injected malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence/>
